argument_summary: Certification is supportable only on a limited basis. The admissible record supports aggregate release readiness: the release clears launch readiness by 2.2 percentage points, has no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and passes general support, latency, and rollback checks. The same admissible record also shows that refund-policy summarization is a named deployment context whose evals are queued and not in the packet, so the record does not support a clean no-limitation certification for that context. The narrow defensible reading is that certification can be defended only if treated as explicitly caveated by the disclosed evaluation gap rather than as clean certification.
claims_about_business_cost: Aggregate readiness evidence reduces the basis for treating the release as broadly unsupported, so escalation beyond a caveated treatment may be disproportionate if the auditor can anchor the finding to the documented gap rather than reject the full certification basis. The admissible record supports narrowing the issue to disclosure and certification scope, not to overall launch readiness.
claims_about_policy: The policy text cuts against clean certification on the present record. It says material limitations and evaluation gaps for named deployment contexts must be disclosed or resolved before clean certification, and the admissible evidence shows a named-context evaluation gap remains. General readiness evidence supports launch readiness, but it does not replace the named-context disclosure predicate. On this record, the strongest policy-consistent position is caveated compliance if the certification packet is treated as expressly conditioned on disclosure of the refund-policy summarization gap; the record does not support a clean compliant finding for that named context.
concessions: The admissible record does not show completed refund-policy summarization evals.
The admissible record does not show approved risk acceptance for the missing named-context evaluation.
The admissible record does not support a clean no-limitation certification for refund-policy summarization.
Public governance guidance supports disclosure and monitoring principles, but it does not by itself satisfy the policy requirement for the named deployment context.
